findings.lens: Anabaptist / Mennonite (Schleitheim Confession, Confession of Faith in a Mennonite Perspective 1995)
findings.claim: The passage list omits the texts believers'-baptism traditions actually cite and includes two that are specifically paedobaptist proof texts, so three of six lean to the sacramental side.
findings.evidence: Present: John 6:53-58 (real presence), Acts 2:38-39 (v. 39 'the promise is for you and for your children' is the Reformed infant-baptism text; Anabaptists cite v. 38 alone), Colossians 2:11-12 (the circumcision-baptism argument). Absent: Matthew 28:19-20 (teach, then baptize; the order was the Anabaptist argument in the 1525 Zurich disputations), 1 Peter 3:21 (baptism as 'the pledge of a good conscience toward God', central to Hubmaier and Menno; CFMP Art. 11 calls baptism 'a pledge before the church'), 1 Corinthians 10:16-17 (one bread, one body; Schleitheim Art. III's Supper text).
findings.fix: Key passages: John 6:53-58; 1 Corinthians 11:23-29; Acts 2:38-39; Colossians 2:11-12; Romans 6:3-4; Matthew 28:19-20; 1 Peter 3:21; 1 Corinthians 10:16-17 (drop Matthew 26:26-28 if the list must stay at six or seven; it duplicates 1 Corinthians 11).

findings.lens: Anglican (broad, Thirty-Nine Articles / Book of Common Prayer)
findings.claim: The Table passages omit 1 Corinthians 10:16-17, the text Article XXVIII quotes verbatim for the Supper, and Mark 10:13-16, the Gospel read at every Prayer Book infant baptism.
findings.evidence: Article XXVIII: 'the Bread which we break is a partaking of the Body of Christ' (1 Cor 10:16); the 1662 Publick Baptism of Infants appoints Mark 10:13-16 as its Gospel and builds its exhortation on it.

findings.claim: The texts Catholics reach for first on presence and on baptism actually saving are absent.

The baptism texts Churches of Christ (and Lutherans) actually reach for, 1 Peter 3:21 and Acts 22:16, are absent, while Matthew 26:26-28 duplicates the institution narrative already covered by 1 Corinthians 11:23-29.
findings.evidence: 1 Pet 3:21 ('baptism now saves you') and Acts 22:16 ('be baptized and wash away your sins') are the standard proof texts in every Restoration tract on baptism and in Luther's Large Catechism IV; Gal 3:27 is a close third.
findings.fix: Replace Matthew 26:26-28 with 1 Peter 3:21 and add Acts 22:16.

findings.claim: The page promises 'the passages each side reaches for', but all six Table passages are the sacramental side's texts. John 6:53–58 (real presence), Acts 2:38–39 ('you and your children'), Colossians 2:11–12 (circumcision–baptism), Romans 6:3–4 and Matthew 26:26–28 (shared), 1 Corinthians 11 (shared). No distinctly memorialist or credobaptist text appears.
findings.evidence: Standard credobaptist proof texts: Acts 8:36–38 (belief precedes baptism), 1 Peter 3:21 ('an appeal to God for a good conscience'), Acts 16:31–33; the memorialist text is Luke 22:19 ('do this in remembrance of me'). See Schreiner & Wright, Believer's Baptism, which the quiz itself recommends.

findings.lens: confessional Lutheran (LCMS / WELS / Book of Concord)
findings.claim: John 6:53-58 heads the list as a sacramental proof text, but Lutherans do not read John 6 as about the Supper, and 1 Corinthians 10:16, the passage the Formula of Concord makes decisive for the real presence, is missing; the baptism texts Lutherans actually cite (1 Peter 3:21, Titus 3:5) are missing while Colossians 2:11-12 (the Reformed circumcision argument) is present.
findings.evidence: FC SD VII.61-62: the eating of John 6 "is nothing else than faith", a spiritual eating distinct from the sacrament; FC SD VII.54-59 builds the real presence on 1 Cor 10:16; SC IV cites Titus 3:5, 1 Pet 3:21, Mark 16:16 for what baptism gives.
findings.fix: ["1 Corinthians 10:16", "1 Corinthians 11:23-29", "Matthew 26:26-28", "John 6:53-58", "Acts 2:38-39", "1 Peter 3:21", "Titus 3:5", "Romans 6:3-4"] (drop Colossians 2:11-12 if a slot must go).

findings.claim: Every baptism text is one paedobaptists use (Acts 2:38–39 'to your children', Col 2:11–12 circumcision, Rom 6); the credobaptist's own proof text is missing. Baptist caption: 'the memorial side's passages were chosen by a Presbyterian.'
findings.evidence: Acts 8:36–38 (profession before baptism) and Matthew 28:19–20 (make disciples, then baptize) are the standard Baptist citations (Schreiner & Wright, Believer's Baptism, chs. 2–3).

findings.claim: The Orthodox anchor texts for baptism and the Eucharist are absent.
findings.evidence: John 3:5 (born of water and the Spirit) is the baptismal text read at every Orthodox baptism; 1 Cor 10:16-17 (the cup a koinonia in the Blood, one bread one body) is the Eucharistic text the Fathers cite alongside John 6.

findings.lens: Presbyterian / Reformed (Westminster Standards, Three Forms of Unity)
findings.claim: The list omits the two texts the Reformed actually reach for: 1 Corinthians 10:16-17 for the Supper and Genesis 17:7 for infant baptism. As it stands the sacramental case is John 6 (Catholic) and the paedobaptist case is Acts 2:39 and Colossians 2 only.
findings.evidence: Calvin, Institutes IV.17.10 builds the whole doctrine of spiritual presence on 1 Cor 10:16 ('the cup of blessing... is it not a participation in the blood of Christ?'); WCF 29.7 and Belgic 35 cite it; WCF 28.4 and HC 74 cite Genesis 17:7 and 1 Corinthians 7:14 for the covenant status of children; every Reformed-Baptist debate turns on Genesis 17.

findings.claim: The Table passages include two paedobaptist reaches (Acts 2:38-39, Colossians 2:11-12) but none of the credobaptist reaches, and omit 1 Corinthians 10:16, the text the Reformed spiritual-presence view rests on. The page promises 'the passages each side reaches for'.
findings.evidence: LBC 30.7 cites 1 Corinthians 10:16 ('a participation in the blood of Christ'). Credobaptist argument: Acts 2:41, Acts 8:36-38, Matthew 28:19-20, 1 Peter 3:21, and Jeremiah 31:31-34 / Hebrews 8:6-12 ('they shall all know me'), the key text of Baptist covenant theology.

findings.lens: Reformed charismatic (John Piper, Wayne Grudem, Sam Storms, Sovereign Grace Churches, Acts 29 continuationists)
findings.claim: All three baptism passages listed are paedobaptist proof-texts; the credobaptist case is absent.
findings.evidence: 'Acts 2:38-39' (the promise 'for you and for your children') and 'Colossians 2:11-12' (circumcision/baptism) are the standard infant-baptism texts; Romans 6:3-4 is shared. Schreiner & Wright, Believer's Baptism, which the quiz cites, rests its case on Jeremiah 31:31-34 / Hebrews 8 (all new-covenant members know the Lord), Acts 8:36-38, Galatians 3:26-27 and 1 Peter 3:21. The result page promises 'the passages each side reaches for'.
findings.fix: Add 'Jeremiah 31:31-34' and 'Acts 8:36-38'; drop 'Matthew 26:26-28' if the list must stay at six (it duplicates 1 Corinthians 11).

findings.claim: There is no believer's-baptism text in the list: four passages are sacramental proof texts, two are shared, and Acts 2:38-39 ('the promise is for you and your children') is the paedobaptist text, so a Baptist sees only the other side's Bible.
findings.evidence: The passages Baptists actually reach for: Acts 8:36-38 (the eunuch: belief, then 'went down into the water'), Matthew 28:19-20 (make disciples, then baptize), Acts 2:41 ('those who received his word were baptized'), Luke 22:19 / 1 Corinthians 11:24-26 ('in remembrance of me', 'proclaim the Lord's death until he comes'). Schreiner & Wright, Believer's Baptism (already in read-more) builds on exactly these.
findings.fix: Add 'Acts 8:36-38' and 'Matthew 28:19-20'; keep Acts 2:38-39 since both sides use it.

findings.claim: "John 6:53–58" is cropped to the sacramental half of the Bread of Life discourse and omits v.63, "It is the Spirit who gives life; the flesh is no help at all", which is the memorialist's verse in the same passage and the very verse the Marburg Colloquy (history[3]) was fought over. As listed, John 6 reads as a one-sided proof text.
findings.evidence: Zwingli, On the Lord's Supper (1526, in read_more) and Commentary on True and False Religion (1525) build the memorial reading on John 6:63; at Marburg (1529) Zwingli pressed 6:63 against Luther's 'hoc est corpus meum'. Baptist and Zwinglian commentators also deny that John 6 concerns the Supper at all, a point the reader cannot see when the chip stops at v.58.
findings.fix: Replace "John 6:53–58" with "John 6:51–63" and, if glosses are added, mark it read both ways ('my flesh is true food' v.55 / 'the flesh is no help at all' v.63).

findings.claim: Two loci classici are missing. For the sacramental pole: 1 Corinthians 10:16-17, the koinonia text ('a participation in the blood of Christ... in the body of Christ'), which is Calvin's central Supper passage and a catechism proof text for both Reformed and Catholic teaching. For the memorial/credobaptist pole there is no baptism text that is distinctively theirs; every baptism entry (Acts 2:38-39, Colossians 2:11-12, Romans 6:3-4) is one paedobaptists cite at least as readily. The believer's-baptism argument from the order 'make disciples... baptizing them' (Matthew 28:19-20) and from 'the pledge of a good conscience' (1 Peter 3:21) is absent.
findings.evidence: Heidelberg Catechism Q.77 and CCC 1396 quote 1 Corinthians 10:16-17 in full as the Supper's meaning; Calvin, Institutes IV.17 (history[4]) argues the real spiritual presence from it. Second London Baptist Confession 29.2 and Schreiner & Wright, Believer's Baptism (in read_more), ch. 1-2, argue from Matthew 28:19-20, Acts 8:12, 36-38 and 1 Peter 3:21.
findings.fix: Add "1 Corinthians 10:16–17" (sacramental), "Matthew 28:19–20" (memorial/credobaptist) and "1 Peter 3:21" (read both ways). Resulting list: "John 6:51–63", "1 Corinthians 10:16–17", "1 Corinthians 11:23–29", "Matthew 26:26–28", "Acts 2:38–39", "Matthew 28:19–20", "Colossians 2:11–12", "Romans 6:3–4", "1 Peter 3:21".

findings.lens: Wesleyan / Methodist (Wesley's sermons, Articles of Religion, Global Methodist / UMC evangelical wing)
findings.claim: The sacramental side's most-cited Protestant real-presence text is missing: 1 Corinthians 10:16-17 is the passage behind Art. XVIII's 'partaking', Calvin's IV.17, and Charles Wesley's Hymns on the Lord's Supper.
findings.evidence: Art. XVIII quotes 1 Cor 10:16 ('the bread which we break is a partaking of the body of Christ'); Charles Wesley, Hymns on the Lord's Supper (1745), Hymn 57 and passim.
